bandReport.notes:
Pages p10-p12 carry Q78-Q100 with no gaps. Layout: p10 = Q78, Q79, Q80 (left) then Q81-Q85 (right); p11 = Q86-Q90 (left) then the Q91-Q92 Direction set (right); p12 = the Q93-Q94 Direction set and the Q95 half of the Q95-Q96 set (left) then Q96, the Q97-Q100 Direction set (right).

SEAM BEFORE: p09 was opened and NOT transcribed. It ends with Q77 complete (stem, both numbered statements, the 'Which of the above statements is/are correct?' line and all four options), and NO Directions block is left open on it, so Q78 starts cleanly and firstComplete is true. Band before this one ends at Q77.

SEAM AFTER: none. p12 is the LAST page of the booklet (13 pages, p00-p12) and the paper GENUINELY ENDS AT Q100 — Q100 prints its stem and all four options ((a) 461, (b) 405, (c) 345, (d) 306) in the right column, with roughly 100 px of blank page below it and no continuation. lastComplete is true.

DIRECTION SETS — four, and all four START inside this band, so this band owns every member of each and none straddles a seam:
  D91-92 (p11 right column) 'Consider the following data for the two (02) items that follow' — age-wise population percentage table.
  D93-94 (p12 left column) 'Consider the following data for the two (02) items that follow' — company expenditure 2011-2017 table.
  D95-96 (p12, block and Q95 in the left column, Q96 at the top of the right column) 'Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow' — budget allocation.
  D97-100 (p12 right column) 'Consider the following for the four (04) items that follow' — 500 candidates failing English/Hindi/Mathematics.
Each block is printed as 'Direction :' (singular, bold), not 'Directions:'. The stimulus is copied verbatim and identically onto every member and each set is contiguous in question number. Note the wording differs between blocks — D91-92 and D93-94 say 'the following DATA for', D95-96 and D97-100 say 'the following for' — that is what is printed and is not a transcription slip.

NO FIGURES ANYWHERE IN THIS BAND. Checked at full page and again on crops. Three things that look like figure candidates and are not: (1) the two printed data tables (D91-92, D93-94) are TABLES and are carried as GFM pipe tables in 'context', not as crops; (2) the D95-96 block says the allocations are 'represented in a pie diagram' but NO pie chart is printed on the page at all — every percentage and the total are given in the block's own prose, so there is nothing to crop (flagged on Q95); (3) the geometry items Q78-Q83, Q86-Q88 are all stated entirely in words, with no accompanying diagram printed. 'hasFigure' is therefore not set on any question in this band.

NO ANSWER KEY. No key, no marked option, no answer table appears on p10, p11 or p12, nor on p09 which was opened for the seam check.

RAISED MIDDLE DOT: this booklet sets decimals with a raised middle dot (12·2, 6·5, 13·8, 300·4, 5·4%). Every one is transcribed as a full stop per the brief. Affected: Q81, Q83, Q86, Q88, Q91-Q100 and both data tables.

CURRENCY: Q95 and Q96 and the D95-96 block print the rupee glyph. Written as 'Rs. ' per the brief's currency rule, matching the convention already in the sibling band files (108 uses of 'Rs.', zero rupee glyphs); no LaTeX macro invented.

EN-DASHES: the D91-92 table's age ranges are printed with en-dashes ('30-34.99' etc.) and are transcribed with the en-dash as printed. It is inside a table cell, so it cannot be confused with the pipe-table separator row.

HIGH-ZOOM CHECKS, all confirming the transcription as written: the D91-92 percentage column (14.00 / 29.75 / 26.25 / 0 / 18.50 / 11.50, including the '0' against 40-44.99 — read at 3x, it really is a bare zero); the D93-94 expenditure column (13.8 / 15.4 / 10.4 / 13.1 / 15.8 / 17.2 / 19.4); the D97-100 counts (500, 30, 75, 50, 15, 17, 17, 5 — the repeated 17 confirmed at 3x); Q85's four fractions (247/108, 251/108, 503/216, 505/216); Q95's four amounts (3.004 / 4.005 / 6.008 / 8.010) and Q96's (360.48 / 300.36 / 240.32 / 180.40).

OPTION LABELS were read off the page separately for each of (a)-(d) on all 23 questions and never inferred from a neighbour, per the brief's warning about the CDS English mis-slotting defect. This matters more than usual on p10 and p12, where several questions set their options in TWO COLUMNS ((a)(b) on one line, (c)(d) on the next) rather than the single stacked column used elsewhere — Q81, Q82, Q84, Q93, Q94, Q97, Q98, Q99, Q100. In every case (b) is the RIGHT-hand option of the first row, not the second item down.

SCAN QUALITY: this is a scan with noticeable bleed-through from the reverse (Hindi text) and occasional specks and stray strokes in the margins and beside option labels. None of it was treated as carrying information; nothing on these pages marks an answer.

NOTHING WAS UNREADABLE and no question had to be left out.

SUBTOPICS: every chapter is a catalog key and every subtopic is one of that chapter's listed subtopics — nothing was invented. Four classification calls worth recording, each a closest fit rather than an exact one. Q82 (relation between the side of an inscribed equilateral triangle and the circumradius) and Q88 (inradius of a triangle from its three sides) are filed under 'Mensuration 2D' / 'Inscribed and Circumscribed Figures'; both could be argued into 'Triangles' / 'Centres of a Triangle', and the mensuration reading was preferred because each asks for a metric relation rather than a property of the centre. Q90 (revolutions of a wheel over a distance) is 'Mensuration 2D' / 'Circle, Sector and Segment' because the quantity used is the circumference; it could be argued into 'Time, Speed and Distance'. Q80 and Q79 are filed under 'Triangles' / 'Angles of a Triangle' although both are really about a ratio of sides forcing an angle. Q97-Q100 are 'Sets' / 'Counting Sets, Subsets and Inclusion Exclusion' rather than 'Data Interpretation', because the stimulus is a prose inclusion-exclusion premise and not a chart or table.

questions.stem:
Let \(D\), \(E\) and \(F\) be the midpoints of the sides \(BC\), \(CA\) and \(AB\) respectively of a triangle \(ABC\). Triangle \(DEF\) is congruent to which of the following triangles?

1. \(AEF\)

2. \(FBD\)

3. \(EDC\)

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
In a triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = AC\) and \(BC\) is produced to \(D\) such that \(\angle ACD = x\), then what is \(\angle BAC\) equal to?
\(ABC\) is a triangle right angled at \(B\) with \(AC = 2BC\). If \(\angle A = x\), then what is \(\angle C\) equal to?
In a triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = 16\) cm, \(AC = 12\) cm and \(AD\) is the bisector of \(\angle A\). If \(BD = 4\) cm, then what is \(CD\) equal to?
An equilateral triangle of side \(x\) is inscribed in a circle of radius \(y\). Which one of the following is correct?
\(ABC\) is a triangle right angled at \(B\). Let \(D\) be the midpoint on \(AC\). If \(BD = 6.5\) cm, then what is \(AB^2 + BC^2\) equal to?

Water is trickling out of a completely filled cylindrical tank of height 1 m and diameter 2 m. Every second a spherical droplet of 1 cm radius trickles down from the bottom of the tank. The tank will be emptied in approximately

The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are in the ratio \(27 : 8 : 1\). The cuboid is melted and recast into a cube. If \(p\) is the surface area of the cuboid and \(q\) is the surface area of the cube, then what is \(p/q\) equal to?
In a right triangle \(ABC\), \(BD\) is perpendicular on hypotenuse \(AC\). If \(AC = 9\) cm and \(AD = 4\) cm, then what is \(AB + BC\) approximately equal to?
In a triangle \(ABC\), \(AD\) is the bisector of \(\angle BAC\). If \(AB = 12\) cm, \(BD = 10\) cm and \(DC = 5\) cm, then what is the perimeter of the triangle?
What is the radius of the circle inscribed in a triangle whose sides are 4 cm, 7.5 cm and 8.5 cm?
In a shower, 5 cm of rain falls. What is the volume of water that falls on 2 hectare area of land?
A bicycle wheel of radius 35 cm makes \(n\) revolutions in moving 11 km. What is the value of \(n\)? (Take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))

Direction : Consider the following data for the two (02) items that follow :

The table below gives the age-wise population percentage of a city :

| Age group | Percentage |
|---|---|
| Below 30 years | 14.00 |
| 30–34.99 | 29.75 |
| 35–39.99 | 26.25 |
| 40–44.99 | 0 |
| 45–49.99 | 18.50 |
| 50 years and above | 11.50 |

The number of persons below the age of 40 years is 10.5 lakhs.
questions.stem: What is the total population of the city (in lakhs)?
flags: The '40–44.99' row of the printed table carries a percentage of 0. Transcribed exactly as printed — not repaired.

Direction : Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow :

The budget allocations represented in a pie diagram under five different heads \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\) and \(E\) are respectively 40%, 18%, 9%, 25% and 8%. The total budget allocation is Rs. 300.4 lakhs.
questions.stem: How much less amount is allocated to \(A\) and \(C\) together as compared to \(B\), \(D\) and \(E\) together?
flags: The Direction block says the allocations are 'represented in a pie diagram', but NO pie chart is printed anywhere on the page — all five percentages and the total are given in the prose of the block itself. hasFigure is therefore not set; there is nothing for the crop operator to take. Same for Q96, which shares this block.

questions.context:
Direction : Consider the following for the four (04) items that follow :

500 candidates appeared in an examination comprising tests in English, Hindi and Mathematics. 30 candidates failed in English only; 75 failed in Hindi only; 50 failed in Mathematics only; 15 failed in both English and Hindi; 17 failed in both Hindi and Mathematics; 17 failed in both Mathematics and English; 5 failed in all three tests.
questions.stem: What is the percentage of candidates who failed in at least two subjects?
questions.subtopic: Counting Sets, Subsets and Inclusion Exclusion
flags: The stimulus prints 17 twice — once for 'both Hindi and Mathematics' and again for 'both Mathematics and English'. Both were re-read at 3x and both are genuinely 17; transcribed as printed, not repaired.
